_doc: Lessons critic r1 G4: the hand audit of every FULL Y1 site lesson against its title AND every CCSS code the site tags it with (data/standards/ccss-math.json descriptors), read from generated items. lessoncheck.py and lessonfit.mjs read it: a FULL lesson with no row, a row whose links are not the lesson's direct links, a row missing one of the lesson's site CCSS codes, or a row for a lesson that is not FULL fails the build. A code the content does not teach is marked 'site tag:' with the reason (owner questions in the report).

K|-|addandsubtractwithin5writtenvertical.title: Add and subtract within 5: add_facts deals + facts with sums 0 to 5 (0 + 4, 3 + 2) and sub_facts deals − facts from 5 or less (5 − 5, 3 − 2), every fact in reach; written vertically (column form): every item is in a column (add_facts: the fact cell with notation vertical; sub_facts: the column facts visual, facts-column-visual), the top number above the sign and the second number, a rule, one answer box; no carrying or borrowing row

ccss.K.OA.A.5: Fluently add and subtract within 5: both operations, every sum and every number taken from at most 5, as fact practice (one fact a cell, answer recalled); standards-audit.js already rules K.OA.A.5 FULL on these two skills at band 5

K|-|composeshapesfromsmallershapes.title: Compose shapes from smaller shapes: compose_shapes joins two drawn pieces and asks which shape they make (two triangles a square, two squares a rectangle, two small triangles a larger triangle, two trapezoids a hexagon); compose_hexagon fills a hexagon outline with pattern blocks (triangles, rhombi or trapezoids)

ccss.K.G.B.6: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes ('Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?'): compose_shapes joins two whole pieces side to side, two triangles making a square (a rectangle with equal sides) and two squares a rectangle, and asks for the larger shape; compose_hexagon fills a larger shape with smaller ones

K|-|bondsto10explorecombinationsthatmake.title: Bonds to 10, explore combinations that make 10: make_ten shows a ten frame with 1 to 9 counters and asks how many more make 10, every pair 1 + 9 to 9 + 1 dealt 5 to 7 times in 50 items

ccss.K.OA.A.4: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10, with a drawing: each item draws the frame with the given number and the pupil records the missing part
ccss.1.OA.C.6: site tag: of the Grade 1 standard only its making-ten strategy is this lesson's content; adding and subtracting within 20 is not (the title bounds the lesson at 10, the Reception step R.B11.S8 'Bonds to 10 (2 parts)')

K|-|compareamountsmorefewersame.title: Compare amounts (more, fewer, same): two pictured groups of 1 to 5 counters, the pupil says which has more, which has fewer, or whether they are the same (about two items in three ask more or fewer, one in three 'Do the groups have the same number of counters?', answered same or not the same)

ccss.K.CC.C.6: Identify whether one group is greater than, less than or equal to another by matching and counting: level 1 draws the two groups with no numbers, so the pupil matches or counts. The standard's parenthesis (groups with up to ten objects) is the Kindergarten end of the range; this Support lesson is judged at its source, Reception Phase 2 (Just Like Me!), whose numbers go to 5, so groups to 5 are the lesson's whole range, and groups to 10 are 'Comparing numbers to 10' (Phase 7), a partial lesson of this file

K|-|comparemass1.title: Compare mass (1): two or three pictured objects, which is heavier, which is lighter

ccss.K.MD.A.2: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute (mass) and describe which has more of it: the pupil picks the heavier or the lighter object and says heavier / lighter (the Say: frame)

K|-|comparemass2.title: Compare mass (2): the same content as Compare mass (1); the site gives the second session no other content (if it is the balance session R.B8.S2, it is partial with build balance: owner question)

ccss.K.MD.A.2: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute (mass) and describe which has more of it: the pupil picks the heavier or the lighter object and says heavier / lighter

K|-|representnumbersto5.title: Represent numbers to 5: the pupil builds each number 1 to 5 (10 of each in 50) with counters on a ten frame

ccss.2.NBT.A.1: site tag: the Grade 2 place-value standard is not this lesson's content (owner question 3). The content is K.CC.B.4 (connect a number to its quantity) and K.CC.B.5's 'given a number, count out that many objects': the pupil reads the numeral and builds that many counters on the frame. The pupil never writes a numeral, so K.CC.A.3 is not claimed
